takeaway: It stores the world as dots, cubes, a skin or soft blobs, and each one trades detail against speed and memory.

selfCheck.question: Why might one robot keep the same mug both as cubes and as a skin?
selfCheck.answer: each does a different job; cubes: one look-up, avoid bumping; skin: smooth accurate shape to plan where fingers go.

sentence: A robot can store the same object in different ways: as dots, as small cubes, as a surface made of triangles, or as soft blobs. Each way is good for a different job, and none is best at everything. For example, cubes make it quickest to check whether something is in the way.

"joins the surface into small flat triangles" (awkward)
"Real ones carry colour and look like a photo" (why grey here)
"They are the newest of the four" (why it matters)
"3,625 dots", "485 cubes", "2,136 triangles", "5,000 soft blobs" (large or small; relation to costs)
"the 15 empty cubes it passed" (could not count 15)
"Far side: no dots" (label points at the dotted part)
"Fingertip" (no arm or hand, only a red ball)

reason: My takeaway names the same four storage forms, but it says each one suits a different job and leaves out the trade between detail and speed and memory, so it only matches part of the point.
